A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ConservationBench and retain the same core evaluation. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 112 VLMs, human performance, and controlled experiments varying prompts, frames and visual input, with detailed results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds prompting and modality controls, cross-benchmark correlations, Cosmos Reason evaluation, and confidence, attention and reasoning-trace analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, frame-selection methods and hybrid answer-matching procedure remain unchanged. Additional prompts and diagnostic measurements are evaluation conditions, rather than a new proposed algorithm or model modification.

E1.justification: Section 4.6 adds score-analysis coverage across nine benchmarks spanning visual perception, physical understanding and video understanding, including BLINK, PhysBench, MLVU and Video-MME. Appendix J adds caption-only and video-plus-caption scenarios. The original four conservation domains remain; the PDFs do not establish that all external benchmarks were rerun.

E2.justification: Appendix N newly evaluates Cosmos Reason, a model post-trained for physical and embodied reasoning. The original 112-model comparison roster in Tables 5–6 is unchanged; models used for caption generation or internal analysis are not additional comparators.

E3.justification: The original factorial evaluation remains, but v2 adds definition and caption controls on 12 models, an abstention option on 10 models, and analyses restricted to the top 15 models. Section 4.7 introduces final-decision-token confidence measurements and attention aggregation across seven frames. These are substantial additions to the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New analyses test task misunderstanding, dependence on forced answers, dilution by weaker models, and the effects of physical post-training. Sections 4.6–4.7 and Appendices O–P additionally examine benchmark relationships, confidence and attention patterns, and a Claude failure trace. v1's behavioral analyses are retained, including former Appendix J as Appendix K.

E5.justification: v2 retains the repeated-measures ANOVA, Bonferroni comparisons and correlation-reporting practices. Additional analyses report new statistical outcomes without introducing repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or a different uncertainty-estimation procedure. The confidence-margin analysis measures model behavior rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 and the original main results are unchanged, including Gemini-2.5-Pro's 69.11% average accuracy and the 98.35% human baseline. v2 adds cross-benchmark correlations of 0.45–0.86, control and Cosmos scores, and confidence, attention and trace findings. For example, new Figure 10 reports caption-only Volume accuracy of 0.014 conserving versus 0.798 non-conserving.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. The added confidence-margin and attention-normalization descriptions specify empirical measurements, without introducing substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and central claim of deficient transformation reasoning remain. The abstract now qualifies the visual-content disadvantage as applying when performance is balanced across conserving and non-conserving scenarios; the discussion more explicitly emphasizes the diagnostic contribution.

C2.justification: v2 moves beyond v1's behavioral explanation to propose confident anchoring on the initial frame, inadequate state updating, and limited prospects for fixing the problem through post-training alone. It adds interpretations about shared abilities across benchmarks and qualifies the mechanistic evidence as preliminary and single-model. Its claimed caption-induced reversal for both Volume and Size exceeds what Figures 10–11 show.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses answer-order counterbalancing and human recruitment and exclusion details: seven recruited, six analyzed. It supplies the conservation-definition prompt, caption-generation and human-verification information, and attention-extraction details. The original hardware and inference appendices remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: New Section 4.6 substantively positions ConservationBench as complementary to naturalistic physical and video benchmarks, using correlations to argue for shared underlying abilities. v2 also relates its findings to physically oriented post-training through Cosmos Reason and adds the corresponding benchmark, model and toolkit citations. The original cognitive-science positioning remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain. v2 revises the abstract, human-study description, discussion and limitations, adds diagnostic subsections and an impact statement, and updates affiliations and publication information. It also removes v1's paragraph describing 96 final-frame tasks, which had no separately reported results.

P2.justification: v2 adds a cross-benchmark heatmap, control-condition charts, top-model plots, confidence distributions, attention heatmaps and a reasoning-trace figure. Existing ranking tables and principal plots are retained, while captions for Figures 2–4 are expanded and appendix displays are relocated or renumbered. The new visual evidence substantially expands the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful diagnostic experiments, preliminary mechanistic evidence and clearer human-study documentation. However, Figures 10–11 contradict the claimed Size bias reversal, and Appendix L's p < 0.0001 claims are unsupported by the stated model-level correlations of 0.591 and 0.362 with only 10 models. These problems affect the new diagnostic conclusions, leaving the net benefit of expanded evidence versus reduced reporting reliability uncertain.
